capstone_format_meta.title: Step 1: Format one event
capstone_format_meta.prompt: Start the final capstone project. In step 1 of 18, Problem: Each event card needs one concise line that helps students understand the category, location, and seat availability without reading raw object fields. Task: Complete only `formatEventMeta(event)` and return one string containing those three values. Expected result: Check Answer confirms that one event can be summarized; nothing is rendered yet.

campus-event-explorer-capstone-concept.title: Campus Event Explorer
campus-event-explorer-capstone-concept.bodyMarkdown:
This capstone combines skills you already practiced. It does not introduce a new JavaScript topic.

**Work one responsibility at a time.** Each project step tells you exactly what to add and what result to expect. Do not build future steps early. When Check Answer passes, the next step starts from that exact working solution.

The application grows through a simple data flow:

`local JSON → validated event array → application state → filtered array → DOM cards`

The interface also makes asynchronous state visible: loading, error, empty, or success.

For example, a reusable rendering helper should do one focused job:

```js
function showMessage(element, message) {
  element.textContent = message;
}
```

Notice that the helper has one input responsibility and one observable result. Use that same discipline throughout the project.
